title: Every customer wants their invoice in a different layout
description: Each account has its own invoice format, so every billing run I take our standard invoice export and rebuild it by hand per customer - different column names, different date formats, different line-item grouping. One wrong charge line and the customer disputes the whole invoice.
current_workflow: Export the billing run from the billing platform
Open the customer's format template
Map our columns onto theirs by hand
Re-check every charge line against the source
Send the invoice and file a copy for Finance

poc.name: Normalise — Every Customer Wants Their Invoice Agent
capabilities: Normalise each customer's layout to the internal schema
Reconcile line by line and isolate the deltas
Explain every delta in one sentence a human can check
Post only what reconciles; hold the rest
poc.guardrail: An unexplained delta blocks the post. Silence is never treated as agreement.
build_steps: Normalise: Export the billing run from the billing platform
Reconcile: Open the customer's format template
Explain: Map our columns onto theirs by hand
Post: Re-check every charge line against the source; Send the invoice and file a copy for Finance

published_agent: Normalise — Every Customer Wants Their Invoice Agent

title: Payments that do not match the invoice get chased by hand
description: When a payment lands that does not reconcile to an invoice, I work backwards through bank statements, credit notes and email to find where the difference came from. Most turn out to be a partial payment or a credit note that nobody applied to the ledger.
current_workflow: Pull the unmatched payments report
Open the invoice and the bank statement side by side
Trace credit notes and partial payments
Email the account owner if it still does not tie out
Post the adjustment and note the reason

poc.name: Normalise — Payments That Do Not Match Agent

Reconcile line by line and isolate the deltas
Explain every delta in one sentence a human can check
Post only what reconciles; hold the rest
poc.guardrail: An unexplained delta blocks the post. Silence is never treated as agreement.
build_steps: Normalise: Pull the unmatched payments report
Reconcile: Open the invoice and the bank statement side by side
Explain: Trace credit notes and partial payments

title: Order forms and contracts get retyped into the CRM
description: A signed order form arrives as a scanned PDF attachment. I read it and retype the terms, dates and pricing into the CRM. Extracting the same fields from a document the customer already filled in is not selling.
current_workflow: Open the signed order form attachment
Read off terms, dates, pricing and entity name
Retype each field into the CRM opportunity
Re-read the document to check nothing was missed
Attach the PDF and hand off to Legal

poc.name: Ingest — Order Forms And Contracts Get Agent
capabilities: Accept PDFs, scans and images without pre-sorting
Pull the named fields out with a confidence score
Check each field against its expected type and range
Route low-confidence extractions to a human queue
poc.guardrail: Below the confidence threshold the agent asks; it never guesses.
build_steps: Ingest: Open the signed order form attachment
Extract: Read off terms, dates, pricing and entity name
Validate: Retype each field into the CRM opportunity
Emit: Re-read the document to check nothing was missed; Attach the PDF and hand off to Legal

published_agent: Ingest — Order Forms And Contracts Get Agent

title: Which clause version is current lives in an email thread
description: Every redline round on a contract arrives as a new document attachment in a long email chain. To answer 'what does the liability clause say right now' I have to read the whole thread and diff the attachments by eye.
current_workflow: Find the latest redline attachment in the thread
Open it against the previous version
Diff the clause by eye
Record the agreed wording in the tracker
Send the next round back to the counterparty

title: Campaign creative waits on three separate sign-offs
description: Every campaign asset needs approval from brand, legal and the product owner. Each review cycle is chased separately, nobody can see who the approval is currently sitting with, and launch dates slip waiting on a gate that the approver did not know was theirs.
current_workflow: Send the asset to brand for sign-off
Chase brand, then forward to legal
Chase legal, then forward to the product owner
Collate the three approvals into the launch checklist
Release the campaign to Sales

poc.name: Check — Campaign Creative Waits On Three Agent
capabilities: Check the request against the policy before anyone is asked
Gather the evidence an approver always ends up asking for
Nudge the one person the request is actually waiting on
Record the decision and the reason against the object
poc.guardrail: The agent prepares and chases decisions. It never makes them.
build_steps: Check: Send the asset to brand for sign-off
Gather: Chase brand, then forward to legal
Nudge: Chase legal, then forward to the product owner
Record: Collate the three approvals into the launch checklist; Release the campaign to Sales

title: Control exceptions need sign-off before every audit
description: Ahead of each audit I chase an approval for every open control exception - who authorised it, until when, and on what basis. The review cycle runs across six teams and the gate stays invisible until the auditor asks.
current_workflow: Pull the open exception register
Identify the owning team for each exception
Request sign-off and chase it
Record the authorisation and its expiry
Assemble the pack for the auditor

title: The account review deck is rebuilt from five dashboards
description: Before every account review I query five dashboards for usage, tickets, invoices, adoption and open actions, then paste the metrics into a slide. The report is stale the moment it is built.
current_workflow: Open each of the five dashboards in turn
Query the account's numbers for the period
Paste the metrics into the review template
Write the commentary from memory
Send the deck to the account team

poc.name: Query — The Account Review Deck Is Agent
capabilities: Run the recurring query set without being asked
Aggregate to the grain the audience actually reads
Narrate what changed and why it plausibly changed
Publish on a schedule to where people already look
poc.guardrail: Every number carries the query and the run time that produced it.
build_steps: Query: Open each of the five dashboards in turn
Aggregate: Query the account's numbers for the period
Narrate: Paste the metrics into the review template
Publish: Write the commentary from memory; Send the deck to the account team

title: Delivery status is a query across four trackers
description: 'Where is this deployment' means opening four trackers and reading them against each other. Building the weekly delivery report is an analyst job that produces a metric nobody can drill into afterwards.
current_workflow: Open each delivery tracker
Reconcile the four views of the same deployment
Build the weekly status report
Circulate it and answer the follow-up questions
Hand the account over to Customer Success

title: Roadmap themes are tallied by hand once a quarter
description: Every quarter an analyst reads through the feedback backlog and tallies the themes in a spreadsheet to produce the roadmap report. By the time the analysis lands, the quarter it describes is over.
current_workflow: Export the quarter's feedback backlog
Read every item and label it by hand
Tally the labels in a spreadsheet
Write the roadmap report from the tallies
Present it and hand the themes to Marketing

title: The same twenty tickets get triaged from scratch every week
description: The same known issues arrive as support tickets week after week, and each one is triaged from the beginning - read the complaint, reproduce it, search whether we have seen it before, then escalate. The SLA clock runs the whole time.
current_workflow: Read the incoming ticket
Try to reproduce the reported behaviour
Search past tickets for the same symptom
Escalate if no known resolution is found
Reply to the customer and close

title: Datacentre asset forms are retyped into the CMDB
description: Hardware arrives with a printed asset form. Someone scans it, reads off the serial, rack position, model and support dates, and retypes all of it into the CMDB. A single mistyped serial makes the record unfindable later.
current_workflow: Scan the printed asset handover form
Read off serial, rack position, model and support dates
Retype each field into the CMDB
Re-check the serial against the document
File the scan against the asset record

title: Supplier warranty documents are retyped into the asset register
description: Each supplier sends warranty certificates as scanned PDF attachments. I read the cover dates, entitlement level and contract reference off the document and retype them into the asset register so renewals can be tracked.
current_workflow: Open the warranty certificate attachment
Read off cover dates, entitlement level and contract reference
Retype the fields into the asset register
Check the reference against the supplier's document
Attach the scan to the register entry

title: Partner spec sheets are retyped into the product catalogue
description: Partners send product spec sheets as PDF documents. To list anything I read off the model names, capabilities and support tiers and retype them into the catalogue, then re-read the sheet to check nothing was missed.
current_workflow: Open the partner spec sheet
Read off model names, capabilities and support tiers
Retype each entry into the product catalogue
Re-read the sheet to check nothing was missed
Publish the catalogue entry

title: Bill Length Reduction Project
current_workflow: Acknowledge task length
Identify main components
Break down into subtasks
Create a checklist of tasks
Ensure each step is clear and concise
Limit steps to no more than eight words per instruction
Verify that there are exactly fourteen instructions in total
Review for logical flow between the steps
Finalize list of imperative short-steps
Ensure each step is actionable and specific
Additional manual step 11
Additional manual step 12
Additional manual step 13
Additional manual step 14

ai_baseline.summary: Develop an automated system to process and summarize bills, reducing their length without losing essential information.
workflow: Identify common phrases used in bill descriptions that can be condensed or replaced with standardized terms
Create a natural language processing model trained on the identified patterns for text simplification
Test and refine the NLP model using sample bills to ensure accuracy of summaries generated
Deploy the system in a controlled environment, monitor its performance, and collect feedback from users
required_data: Sample bill documents with varying lengths and complexities for training data
Feedback forms or surveys to gather user experience insights post-deployment
risks: The NLP model may not accurately capture the nuances of legal language, leading to loss of critical information in summaries.
User resistance due to unfamiliarity with automated systems or distrust in AI'decisions.
ai_baseline.why_ai: AI can efficiently process large volumes of text and learn from examples, making it ideal for summarizing repetitive manual tasks like bill length reduction without sacrificing accuracy or essential details.
